newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton ranged ahead of advisory panel meet.
newsitem.headline: India cotton ranged ahead of advisory panel meet.

text.p: Cotton prices were steady in a narrow price band on local markets, dealers said on Monday.
Mill buying was dull and volumes thin ahead of a scheduled meeting of the Cotton Advisory Board later in the day.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi was steady at 780/820 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned was quiet at 1,400/1,625 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) was steady at 11,400/11,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"The Cotton Advisory Board had estimated cotton crop for 1996/97 at 15.50 million bales (170 kg each) in its last meeting two months ago," one broker said.
"Now the Board may lift estimates to 16/16.50 million bales looking at the late range in the producing centres which has boosted crop prospects," one broker said.
"So far in the current year, Indian government has allowed export of 1.22 million bales and Advisory Board may recommend more export, going by the sluggish price trend in the recent days," he added.
